name: Downstroke
description: Strumming down through the strings toward the floor. The foundation of almost every strumming pattern.

name: Upstroke
description: Strumming up through the strings toward the ceiling, usually lighter and hitting fewer strings than a downstroke.

name: Alternate strumming
description: Keeping a continuous down-up hand motion and choosing which strokes actually hit the strings — the basis of real strumming patterns.

name: Palm muting
description: Resting the side of the picking-hand palm lightly on the strings near the bridge to shorten and soften the notes.

name: Hammer-on
description: Sounding a higher fretted note by tapping a finger down onto the string without picking again.

name: Pull-off
description: Sounding a lower note by pulling a fretting finger off the string with a slight flick, without picking again.

name: Slide
description: Sliding a fretting finger from one fret to another while keeping pressure on, connecting the two notes smoothly.

name: Bend
description: Pushing or pulling a fretted string sideways to raise its pitch.

name: Vibrato
description: Rapidly, subtly bending a note up and down to add expression and sustain.

name: Fingerpicking
description: Plucking individual strings with the picking-hand fingers/thumb instead of strumming with a pick.

name: String muting
description: Preventing unwanted strings from ringing, using either hand — essential for clean chords.

name: Barre chords
description: Using one finger to press down multiple strings at once, letting a chord shape move anywhere on the neck.
